document_title: When the control record arrives: a finite-error memory law for one quantum payload
status: Scoped primary comparison and provenance manifest; no exhaustive literature or historical-priority claim.
error_convention: All analytic channel errors are half diamond distance. Numerical Choi residuals are half trace distances of normalized Choi states, not evaluated diamond norms.
claim_boundaries: The selected result is a programmed-source metadata-timing construction and a quantitative payload-memory theorem.
No historical priority, first late-choice memory phenomenon, first measurement-relative compression model, or new small-bias/expander machinery is claimed.
No small-memory near-linear decoder or universal memory lower bound for the homogeneous weak partial-SWAP stream is claimed; that operation remains unresolved.
The scalar receiver companion excludes only one tracial receiver qubit with predetermined partial-SWAP updates, plus an arbitrary final decoder.
The early-selector receiver is an environment-assisted correction operation with paid timing, source coherence, initialization, local control, routing, calibration and error budgets.
The source, gap and metadata costs of the uniform-Pauli, small-bias-Pauli and imported local-expander families cannot be interchanged.
Finite numerical execution is not laboratory validation; equally informed established baselines receive the same physical access.
metadata_policy: Titles, author spellings and source URLs follow primary records where available. Null fields indicate metadata not established in this packaging check, not nonexistence. Individual authorship of accepted internal packages is not inferred from a repository owner.
